title: DevX Golden Trace & Execution Replay Playbook
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Summary
=======

This playbook defines the DevX 'Golden Trace' and Execution Replay workflows used by Redwood support, SDK, and runtime teams to reproduce intermittent, customer-facing failures deterministically. It codifies what to capture, how to store a gold trace, and a step-by-step replay and remediation loop that maps traces to canonical fixes.

Why we need a Golden Trace
-------------------------
- Intermittent production bugs (tokenization regressions, streaming discontinuities, racey cache state) are hard to reproduce locally.
- Golden traces are time-bounded, end-to-end recordings of a problematic request path that contain the minimal information needed to deterministically replay behavior against the runtime and SDK layers.
- A good golden trace reduces time-to-resolution from hours/days to typically under 90 minutes for known classes of issues.

Scope and definitions
---------------------
- Golden trace: an immutable artifact capturing input, SDK-side context, request metadata, and session-scoped runtime artifacts (KV-cache keys, model selection decisions) sufficient to re-run the request.
- Execution replay: the process and tooling that consumes a golden trace and replays it deterministically against a selected target (local shim, staging runtime, dedicated replay cluster).
- Canonical fix: a documented code/config change with a small runnable reproducer and owner.

Capture checklist (what to include)
----------------------------------
1) Customer-visible inputs (obligatory):
   - Original HTTP request payload as sent by customer (body)
   - SDK version and commit hash
   - Client configuration flags (timeout, retry/backoff policy, streaming enabled, prefetch/bundling params)
2) Runtime routing/selection metadata:
   - Model id and pinned version
   - Route id, datacenter/region, and pool id (if Dedicated)
   - Fallback decisions (if any) with timestamps
3) Telemetry and trace ids:
   - Request id, trace id, span ids (if present)
   - SDK correlation id and token-level sequence markers
4) Streaming artifacts (if applicable):
   - Ordered stream fragments, with sequence numbers and byte offsets
   - Partial content markers and end-of-stream flag
5) Deterministic seeds and KV cache snapshot (when available):
   - RNG/temperature seeds used by model sampling (if set)
   - KV cache keys relevant to the request and per-key sizes (not full token content unless requested)
6) System-level context:
   - Server-side execution timeline (timestamps of major phases: routing, queueing, start-of-inference, emit-token ranges)
   - Observability logs (error/warning lines) clipped to +/- 30s around the request
7) Customer consent flag and redaction plan:
   - Indicate whether customer approved full payload capture or requires redaction

Storage and retention policy
---------------------------
- Golden traces are stored in the DevX replay bucket (s3://redwood-devx-golden-traces) with ACLs restricted to support, runtime, and security.
- Naming convention: yyyyMMdd-<request-id>-<short-reason>-<env>.tgz
- Retention: default 90 days; extendable to 365 days with security approval for regulatory investigations.
- Labels and indexing: attach metadata (customer_id, region, SDK-version, model-id, issue-tag) for quick search.

Replay targets and tooling
-------------------------
- Local shim (recommended first step): developer uses devx-replay-cli to replay a trace against a local runtime container. Good for rapid iteration.
- Staging runtime: for environment parity, replay against the latest staging model bundle. Useful when the issue depends on infra config.
- Dedicated replay cluster: for high-fidelity replays that require GPU-level determinism (quantization/backing kernels). Only used for P0/P1 bugs.

Commands and examples
---------------------
- Capture helper (run inside SDK):
  curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' \ 
    -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/_internal/captureTrace 
    -d '{"request_id":"req_12345","capture_level":"full"}'

- devx-replay-cli (replay locally):
  # download trace artifact then:
  devx-replay --trace /tmp/20270210-req_12345-stream-abort-prod.tgz --target local --runtime-image redwood/runtime:dev-20270201 \
    --env-vars 'SDK_DEBUG=1' --mount-keys /tmp/kv-snapshot.json

- replay to staging with model pinning:
  devx-replay --trace /tmp/trace.tgz --target staging --model sha256:abcdef --capture-logs --output /tmp/replay-output

Deterministic replay tips
------------------------
- Ensure the runtime image matches the kernel / quantization build used in production. Check the runtime build-id in the trace metadata.
- When sampling differences appear, confirm seed propagation: many SDKs default to non-deterministic seeding; customers who want deterministic replays should enable 'seed' in client-side config.
- For streaming mismatches: replay with identical chunk sizes and network pacing. devx-replay has a --pacing-ms option to emulate network behavior.

Triage workflow (step-by-step)
-----------------------------
1) Customer submits ticket with request id or SDK trace id.
2) Support captures a golden trace (use Capture checklist) or requests customer's artifact upload to the DevX bucket.
3) Support performs a local quick-replay. If the issue reproduces, attach logs and escalate to SDK/runtime owner.
4) If not reproducible locally, replay to staging. Record diff between production trace and staging replay (token diffs, timing diffs).
5) If staging reproduces, create a bug and mark P1/P2 depending on impact. Add the golden trace link to the ticket.
6) Create an executable reproducer (smallest possible shim) and a PR template that includes: steps to run the repro, expected vs actual, and telemetry pointers.
7) Owner lands fix and attaches a post-rollback golden trace showing resolution.

Mapping traces to canonical fixes (patterns)
-------------------------------------------
- Tokenization drift: compare tokenizer versions recorded in the trace header. Canonical fix: lock tokenizer version in SDK and add a compatibility test.
- Streaming gap at chunk boundary: often a client-side buffering change. Canonical fix: update SDK stream-assembler to use boundary-aware flush.
- Model-quality regressions: tie to model-version in trace. Canonical fix: update model rollout policy and create a prompt-based eval that catches the regression.
- Latency spike / queueing anomaly: identify queue wait timestamps; canonical fix: autoscale policy tuning or circuit-breaker configuration.

Security, PII, and redaction
---------------------------
- Default policy: redact customer PII from stored traces. Allowed fields: request id, model id, SDK version, timing metadata. Customer consent required to store full prompt content.
- Redaction checklist: run the redaction tool as part of capture pipeline; generate a redaction-report and store it alongside the trace.
- Access controls: trace artifacts are tagged as 'restricted' when full payload retained. Security approval required to share externally.

SLOs and operational metrics for the Playbook
--------------------------------------------
- Mean time to first-replay (MTFR): target <= 60 minutes for tickets marked "debuggable".
- Fraction of tickets with usable golden trace at intake: target >= 75%.
- Replay reproducibility rate (local + staging): target >= 80% for issues classified as deterministic.
- Owner assignment within 4 hours for P1 reproductions.

Ownership and roles
-------------------
- Support: capture initial trace, perform first-replay, file ticket with trace link.
- DevX Tools (team): maintain devx-replay-cli, stub containers, and replay infra.
- Runtime owners: investigate runtime-level failures and own fixes that touch kernels/quantization.
- SDK owners: investigate client-side bugs and maintain SDK-level determinism flags.

Onboarding checklist for new engineers
------------------------------------
1) Read this playbook and the devx-replay-cli README.
2) Run the local replay example against the included sample trace (sample_trace.tgz) and verify output.
3) Pair with Support on a real ticket capture and walk through end-to-end replay.

Common pitfalls and mitigation
-----------------------------
- Pitfall: Capturing oversized traces that include entire datasets.
  Mitigation: Enforce size limits on capture; request targeted snapshots instead.
- Pitfall: Missing runtime build-id in trace metadata -> non-reproducible.
  Mitigation: Required schema field; capture pipeline rejects traces without build-id.
- Pitfall: Developers assuming replays are always byte-for-byte identical.
  Mitigation: Educate on non-determinism sources (sampling, kernel order) and provide diff tooling that focuses on clinically relevant differences.

Appendix A — Minimal trace JSON header example
----------------------------------------------
{
  "request_id": "req_12345",
  "sdk_version": "js-2.4.1",
  "runtime_build": "runtime-20270201-gpu-v2",
  "model_id": "open-llm-x:20270120",
  "timestamp": "2027-02-10T15:23:42Z",
  "capture_level": "partial",
  "consent_flag": "redacted"
}
